answer: Cross-agent dependency canyon.** Each new agent must be cited as a dependency by two existing agents whose own reputation score drops if the newcomer misbehaves, creating a loss canyon for the recruiters. A clone therefore imposes a ripple of collateral damage on real identities. Every identity also pays a recurring liveness proof tied to unique hardware entropy, and failed proofs emit a public echo that decays referral scores. Cost per clone: hardware attestation plus reputation damage to two established agents.
